reason: A background command's results callback was projected into provider history as an invalid nebula.tool-result/v2 dict (no tool_version, extra output/stdout fields), so the history sanitizer replaced it with the pre-v2 omission notice and the model never saw the result. The results webhook now stores posted stdout/output as tool-call artifacts in the same transaction as the execution update (automation_runtime.accept_results), and chat materializes the callback as a valid bounded v2 receipt with artifact references; the missing-callback failure envelope now names its tool call and captured output. The selection covers the whole callback journey (test_process_results_webhook: webhook route, accept, resume through start_provider_turn/provider admission, the next provider request, tool_output.read of the posted artifact, failed callback, producer ending without callback, startup reconciliation of settled and waiting callbacks), the automation runtime whose accept path changed (test_automation_runtime), the provider tool loop that consumes and replays tool results (test_chat_tool_loop), the pending-callback turn API, and the waiting-callback persistence guard.
exclusions: Full suites are not approved and are excluded. No UI, Playwright, native or frontend code changed, so those layers are empty; the callback step's artifact list reuses the existing tool-artifact inspector. Note: tests/v3/test_automation_runtime.py::test_host_scope_expiry_closes_running_commands is timing-sensitive; it failed locally in file order under load average ~10 on both this branch and pristine origin/main c273ea2, and passes on both at normal load (42/42 on origin/main 9718333 and on this branch). The complete-callback and missing-callback journeys were also exercised against a scratch Core with a real OpenRouter model in host execution mode.
